scenario.name: Logix / AION alternative history
scenario.alternative_scenario: The events and market outcomes described here belong to the fictional alternative timeline.
scenario.time_model: A time traveler can use future knowledge and equipment to intervene in earlier decades.

principles.title: Identity and future knowledge
principles.description: Vincent gains time-travel powers at age nineteen in 2025 and operates in the past as Adam Pleskot. His foreknowledge remains secret.

principles.title: Investment advantage concealed by analysis
principles.description: Foreknowledge drives unusually successful investments; data analysis and prediction algorithms provide a public explanation.

principles.title: Compete for the personal-computing standard
principles.description: Compete with IBM, present products at NCC from 1978 and COMDEX from 1979 onward, and manufacture at the maximum feasible scale to achieve standard-setting market coverage.

principles.title: Build a complete platform
principles.description: Develop customer trust and a loyal network of users, software developers and peripheral manufacturers through integrated hardware, software, training and support.

principles.title: Separate future-equipped facility
principles.description: A secret facility outside the three companies uses equipment brought from the 2020s for chip design and lithography.

principles.title: Changed availability of historical personnel
principles.description: Gordon Letwin never joins Microsoft; Tim Paterson never develops QDOS or becomes available to Microsoft in this timeline.

principles.title: Engineering and manufacturing organization buildout
principles.description: Hire staff, establish software-development environments, computer manufacturing and R&D, and a conservative semiconductor operation.

principles.title: Other companies monitor the market
principles.description: Actively monitor Logix/AION without significant decisions or actions yet.

principles.title: US personal-computer market expansion
principles.description: Contribute through product availability, computer popularization, seamless peripherals and accessible interfaces.

outcomes.description: US personal-computer market is larger than in the base scenario.

principles.title: Open platform and independent suppliers
principles.description: Logix alone develops the Apple II and S-100 expansion cards; these demonstrate Adam’s ecosystem intentions and are not DRI obligations. Apple cards expose FlexiBUS and video to native Apple software. CP/M-6502 is deferred, with no product, schedule or cost commitment. Published interfaces and affordable developer access permit competing software, cards, peripherals and monitors. AION retains Abacus, C tools, Business Tools, AIONix and the existing Pulse offering; DRI licenses CP/M independently. BPI operates independently under its own brand from the cooperation period. Any further ownership separation around 1985 remains a future transaction, not the beginning of operational independence or a completed buyout.

conventions.dates: Previously confirmed events retain exact days. New 1974 DRI founding retains year precision (late-year qualifier in its title); SMC agreement and initial sales retain month precision. Equal start/end partial dates identify one milestone within that period, not a whole-period process. Never infer a confirmed day from plotting geometry.
conventions.plans: Targets, offers and future rights are distinguished from completed actions.
conventions.naming: Stable actor/product identifiers; aliases retain spelling variants.
conventions.event_structure: Events use date, participants, actions, outcomes, agreement_terms, metrics, product_refs and related_event_refs. Processes use period and phase_refs instead of event_type/date; phase_refs identify narrative context, not asserted start/end dates.
conventions.provenance: This JSON structures the narrative; product specifications remain in the technical catalog. The technical catalog is an author-facing, all-years reference, not a contemporaneous press kit. All 1979 public and partner-facing next-generation references must follow the disclosure policy in ncc_1979_campaign.json; internal identifiers do not establish public product names.
conventions.phase_order: Eight consecutive inclusive calendar phases from 1972-01-01 through 1981-11-18. Point events are assigned by their confirmed dates and sorted chronologically. The 2025-12-07 origin remains an explicit prologue associated with phase one, outside its calendar period. Processes are listed separately in their contextual phases; the explicit 1973–1975 investment expansion spans phases one and two.

phases.title: Adam studying and investing on stock market

actions.description: Gains the ability to travel through time at age nineteen.

events.title: Arrival and assumption of Adam’s identity

actions.description: Travels to January 1972 and assumes the identity of a similar-looking nineteen-year-old in the UK before the death is noticed.

outcomes.description: The original Adam had graduated from high school and died with his parents in a car accident. Vincent is subsequently called Adam.

events.title: Lottery win and US relocation preparations

actions.description: Leaves the UK, wins Germany’s LOTTO 6aus49 using foreknowledge, exchanges the winnings and prepares to move to the US.

events.title: Move to the US and start of NYSE investing

actions.description: Moves to the US and begins investing and speculating on the NYSE using secret foreknowledge.

outcomes.description: Rapid multiplication of Adam’s wealth through NYSE investing and speculation.

actions.description: Starts an office with three workers, a PDP-11/40 and three terminals. Workers manually capture New York Times stock prices, sales, other statistics and company/market sentiment measures.

outcomes.description: Data supports analysis and prediction; algorithms serve as a cover for unusual investment success.

actions.description: Formalize and finance DRI before Logix exists. Gary leads CP/M engineering, Dorothy operations, and Adam capital, product strategy and OEM relationships. Begin earlier hardware abstraction and stable documented interfaces; implement optional ROM, memory and TUI services progressively. Precise founding month/day remains unspecified.

agreement_terms.description: DRI owns CP/M and DRI-funded improvements; licenses competing OEMs on predictable non-exclusive terms. Logix later pays OEM license and platform-engineering charges.
Gary and Dorothy together retain 60% on a fully diluted basis; their internal allocation is unspecified.
Adam receives 30% for his capital commitment and founding contribution.
Reserve for future employees; not an issued voting block.
Adam commits $250,000 nominal 1974 USD over two years: $150,000 at formation and $100,000 in scheduled installments. Company capital, not a CP/M purchase price or per-copy manufacturing cost.
Technical leadership and neutral licensing protected; Logix-related transactions independently reviewed. Expansion cards and chip licensing remain Logix/AION work, not DRI deliverables.

phases.title: Preparing first products and their ecosystem

actions.description: Establishes Logix Tech in San Jose for software and computers, AION Labs in Cambridge for semiconductors, and AION Software in Copenhagen for business applications and compilers.
Brings CAD and laser-lithography equipment from the 2020s and establishes a facility separate from the three companies.

outcomes.description: Future chip-design tools supplement a publicly conservative semiconductor operation.

actions.description: Within the partnership founded in late 1974, agree the Aurelia OEM implementation and freeze ROM/banking, FlexiBUS, display and optional TUI interface requirements. This is not first contact with DRI.

agreement_terms.description: DRI retains the right to implement the TUI libraries and FlexiBUS support in CP/M versions for non-Logix computers.

events.title: Investment and cooperation offer to independent BPI Systems

actions.description: Adam proposes cash investment and a separately incorporated BPI Systems venture, retaining the BPI brand and independent management, with development cooperation from AION and distribution cooperation from Logix.

outcomes.description: Proposed BPI management retains product, licensing and specialist-support responsibility. AION engineers assist the C port, database and TUI implementation under agreement. The offer is not evidence of a completed equity transaction.

agreement_terms.description: Cash offered to BPI owners.

Original proposed founder stake in the separately incorporated BPI venture; not a final cap table or evidence of a completed investment. BPI remains independently operated, even if Adam becomes an investor.

actions.description: BPI and Adam agree operational cooperation: independent BPI management, brand, application ownership, licences and specialist support; AION engineering assistance and Logix distribution/training. The earlier $150,000 and 33% offer remains a proposal; no final ownership closing is asserted. Date selected for the alternative scenario.
Recruits Gordon Letwin from his then-current employer.

outcomes.description: Letwin never joins Microsoft in this scenario.

actions.description: Recruits Tim Paterson.

outcomes.description: Paterson does not develop QDOS and is unavailable to Microsoft.

actions.description: Agree OEM purchasing/manufacturing arrangements for bare MP-40 mechanisms to receive FlexiBUS controllers.

events.title: AIONix preliminary architecture and portability work

actions.description: Begin funded exploratory architecture, C portability and future ERA operating-system work before Aurelia launch. Preserve CP/M maintenance and the Aurelia release team. The September 12 agreement later formalises ownership, staffing and funding; preliminary work does not move product availability.
Arrange computer sales through ComputerLand as the planned primary channel.

agreement_terms.description: Retailer margin of 20–30%.

events.title: BPI business and accountant pilot programme

actions.description: Target 10–15 pilot businesses and several accounting practices; reconcile results against existing records. Validate representative data volumes, disk/RAM budgets, posting, corrections, backup/restore and supported payroll jurisdictions before launch claims. Date selected for the alternative scenario.

Establishes the Academy company and prepares rented facilities for an initial five-city US programme; publicly presented at the June 5 Aurelia premiere. City names and first course dates remain unspecified; capacity expands with demand.
Newspaper and business-press teasers introduce Aurelia and the personal-assistant promise; coming this spring, followed by June 5 launch date; brochure and invitation requests.

Cinematic TV commercial and explanatory print advertisements; prioritise markets with demonstration, support and Academy coverage. Proposed Michael Douglas therapy-session reveal; casting remains subject to agreement. No AI or unhealthy-dependency claim.

events.title: Press, dealer and launch preparation (late May into early June)

actions.description: Press previews, dealer/staff preparation, launch invitations, television-station outreach and complete venue rehearsal. Month precision preserves the planning window; no exact preview date is asserted.

events.title: BPI launch qualification and dealer preparation

actions.description: Qualify all advertised launch modules and a modest summary export to Abacus. Train instructors and dealers, publish requirements and support boundaries, and prepare a joint press preview. Measured capacity and final jurisdiction coverage remain acceptance gates, not invented results. Date selected for the alternative scenario.

phases.title: Aurelia premiere and first months of sales

actions.description: Premieres Aurelia: startup, common editing, safe peripheral attachment, Business Tools, eight-minute Abacus demonstration, then seven-minute BPI partner demonstration. DRI, MPI and the head of BPI speak in the seven-minute partners section. Academy and dealer configurations follow. Total 44 minutes before questions; see aurelia_1978_campaign.json.

outcomes.description: Platform includes AION software, peripherals, support, developer programs and Academy training.

Academy Fundamentals offers two days of hands-on learning before purchase; 50% tuition credit valid six months toward one Aurelia, redeemable at Academy or participating dealers reimbursed by Logix. Orders accepted at training; no purchase obligation. Locations, tuition and first class dates must be published once selected.

events.title: Independent BPI Systems launches Aurelia applications

actions.description: BPI presents its separately licensed five-module application family immediately after Abacus. Its head then joins Gary Kildall and MPI in the partners section, explaining BPI ownership of products, independent management and cooperation with Adam, AION and Logix. No personal identity for the head is invented.

outcomes.description: Dealer configurations combine separately identified suppliers; BPI is not a Logix division. A documented BPI-to-Abacus summary export supports planning without modifying accounting records.

events.title: NCC technical sessions, professional filming and free television distribution

actions.description: Logix holds architecture/open-peripheral and C IDE/SDK sessions plus hands-on demos. A professional team records every Logix NCC presentation, including partner segments and Q&A. After NCC, edit attractive features, news excerpts and full presentations and supply cleared broadcast material free to any willing television station, including normal copies/dispatch. Stations decide whether and when to air it; no guaranteed coverage. Continue Academy courses, dealer demos and practical advertising.

events.title: BPI training and direct sales begin

actions.description: Academy begins BPI-authorised practical courses and direct distribution under a cooperation agreement. Dealers handle first-line installation enquiries, BPI handles software defects and specialist support, and Logix supports hardware. Tuition, setup services and software licences remain separate.

Start independent second-source manufacturing and sales cooperation after Aurelia’s premiere. AION transfers working reference silicon, SMC-compatible ready-to-use masks, process know-how and production-test specifications; SMC supplies process/mask requirements and performs its own wafer fabrication. Logix supplies reference boards, system tests and initial purchase commitments.

agreement_terms.description: Non-exclusive independent manufacturing and sales rights for the four named chip types, including sales to Logix competitors. ERA CPU designs and unrelated chips are excluded.

AION adapts mask sets to SMC’s agreed process and lithography equipment, supplies revisions/test structures and sends engineers to assist DRAM retention, sensing, refresh and buffered-controller timing qualification. Masks alone do not transfer a process.

AION/Logix funds transfer engineering, mask revisions and qualification; SMC earns manufacturing margin and pays negotiated royalties on external sales. Amounts and minimum purchase volumes remain unspecified.
First qualified independent chip sales targeted for October 1979; family-wide timing depends on per-part qualification, especially video RAM. Volume/yield ramp continues into 1980.

actions.description: Respond to Aurelia with a coordinated search for accounting, spreadsheet and database partners, engineering access and demonstration systems. Disk II development already predates Aurelia; this is a change in software/commercial priority, not the invention of disk support.

Begin BPI dealer qualification and accountant demonstration access, permission-based case studies and defined paid setup assistance. Each initial Academy centre has access to a BPI specialist; recruit or train ahead of demand. Date selected for the alternative scenario.

events.title: AIONix development programme and ownership formalised

actions.description: Formalise the AIONix programme begun in February 1978: joint ERA development in assembler and C, funded by AION. Existing ownership, equity and future porting-right terms remain.

agreement_terms.description: DRI dedicates staff and operating-system expertise alongside AION Software.
AION Software covers DRI costs and expenses.
AION Software owns and controls the AIONix roadmap.
Gary Kildall receives Logix equity in tranches.
DRI obtains rights to port AIONix to non-ERA processors in 1982.
DRI may reuse key AIONix components, but not Logix computer architecture or bus/I/O standards.
AIONix department moves from Copenhagen to Logix offices near DRI headquarters.

This separate AIONix agreement does not transfer CP/M ownership or restrict DRI’s independent CP/M OEM business. Existing AION ownership, Gary’s 8% Logix grant and the 1982 AIONix non-ERA porting right remain; replacing those specific terms requires a separate decision.

actions.description: Prepare complete-system quotations, repeatable business-workflow demonstrations and introductory customer lessons. Initial implementation is selective, not an instantly nationwide training network.
Expand the July business-software initiative into partner negotiations for disk-based accounting, spreadsheets and databases; seek independent software alternatives to AION.

Run year-end preparation workshops and module-upgrade demonstrations. Specify payroll update coverage and maintenance terms. Customer data remains under customer control; referrals do not imply an accountant endorsement without consent. Date selected for the alternative scenario.

events.title: Adam opens confidential Model II cooperation talks

actions.description: After Aurelia launch and growing dealer sales, Adam demonstrates Abacus and proposes an official Model II CP/M configuration plus FlexiBUS in return for an AION-funded Abacus adaptation. Talks occur during the scenario early-design window; no historical design-freeze date is asserted. Confidential talks have no immediate mass-market demand effect.
Begin external OEM implementations, developer documentation and qualification of portable TUI/FlexiBUS extensions, executing the portability policy established at DRI founding.

events.title: Tandy, Logix, DRI and AION sign Model II cooperation agreement

actions.description: Tandy commits to officially selling/supporting CP/M and a qualified FlexiBUS option for Model II, supplies engineering access and distributes Abacus. DRI supplies CP/M and required platform services. Logix supplies interface documentation, reference engineering and initial chips. AION funds the port, corrects incompatibilities, qualifies and maintains the Model II edition. Tandy keeps native video, keyboard, disk architecture, legacy ports, branding, sales and first-line support. No Logix video or CP/M-6502 commitment.

agreement_terms.description: Non-exclusive software and interface licenses; Tandy can manufacture or source compatible peripherals. Exact royalties, engineering payments and minimum software purchases remain unspecified.

Abacus acceptance covers native display/keyboard, documented editing behaviour, CP/M services, printing, shared document format, save/reopen and measured RAM/worksheet/performance limits on a 64 KB configuration. No automatic Aurelia binary or identical-capacity claim.

Use a Model II-specific internal FlexiBUS option board, provisionally two ports, rather than force a mainboard or video redesign. Preserve existing Tandy interfaces. Slot, power, timing and quiescent-attachment qualification are required.

Radio Shack owns the customer relationship and delivers demonstrations/training; AION handles software defects and updates. No Academy attendance or Logix-branded peripherals required. Initial AION silicon supply must not depend on unqualified October 1979 SMC parts.

events.title: Model II compatibility design baseline agreed

actions.description: Reserve an internal option-board slot and interface/power budget before the scenario design baseline is closed. Freeze CP/M BIOS responsibilities, native display/keyboard adapter and the FlexiBUS connector plan. This review is an invented alternate-history engineering milestone, not a claim about the real Model II freeze date.

events.title: BPI customer results and dealer expansion

actions.description: Expand demonstrations and qualified support using verified customer results. Promote module-to-suite upgrade credit. BPI Model II support is a separate future negotiation; the existing Tandy agreement covers Abacus only. Date selected for the alternative scenario.
Develop an Apple II accounting offering with Peachtree while separately pursuing spreadsheet and database suppliers. Peachtree is not treated as a substitute for Abacus by itself.
Start a partnership for an Apple II business offering.

outcomes.description: In the scenario, VisiCalc is less advanced in spreadsheet size and available features.

events.title: Logix and Apple agree limited technical cooperation

actions.description: Requests documentation, test machines and compatibility assistance for native Apple II FlexiBUS, disk interoperability and Logix video products.
Agrees to limited technical cooperation and compatibility assistance.

outcomes.description: Apple accepts Logix-funded native expansion as a way to increase installed Apple II utility, with separate branding/support and no requirement to adopt the full Logix platform; its own peripheral strategy continues.

agreement_terms.description: Access to relevant Apple II documentation and machines.
Assistance with compatibility testing.
Engineering consultation on Apple II peripherals and Disk II compatibility.
Logix retains hardware and software design/development responsibility.

events.title: Model II CP/M and Abacus prototype review

actions.description: Review prototype CP/M boot, Tandy disk/printer BIOS, native TUI adapter and Abacus document interchange. Resolve ROM/banking assumptions and measure available RAM on the 64 KB target. FlexiBUS prototype is specific to the Tandy bus, not a plug-in S-100 card.

events.title: Independent OEM and peripheral engineering briefings

actions.description: Begin confidential briefings and engineering-kit evaluations. Prioritise North Star and Vector Graphic as prospects; approach Cromemco, Altos, Intertec and Heath selectively. Invitations are not signed agreements or qualified products. This day is a selected scenario milestone.

Participating dealers promote Apple II/Disk II business configurations, demonstrations and introductory lessons; Apple pursues spreadsheet distribution/development support separately from Peachtree accounting. No completed VisiCalc release or finished March 1980 Apple–Peachtree package is pulled into spring 1979.

Release documented, optional CP/M Platform Extensions for non-Logix manufacturers: TUI, capability discovery and FlexiBUS adapters. Ordinary CP/M remains usable without these facilities; hardware and application resource requirements still apply.

outcomes.description: The CP/M ecosystem retains an opportunity to expand.

actions.description: Alongside the existing DRI portable-extension release, publish separate CP/M application, FlexiBUS peripheral and optional Logix display compatibility profiles, reference-driver and test access, non-exclusive implementation principles and support-roadmap requirements. Exact fees and support duration remain to be settled. This day is a selected scenario milestone.

Invite computer, software and peripheral suppliers to test named configurations and document failures before public demonstrations. Supplier attendance and passing results must be verified; no announcement of an unsigned OEM. This day is a selected scenario milestone.

events.title: Model II announced with planned CP/M, FlexiBUS and Abacus offering

actions.description: Publicly announce Model II and the planned officially supported CP/M/Abacus configuration and FlexiBUS option. Preserve the historical late-May announcement window, June NCC demonstrations and October US delivery window. Announcements and orders are not completed computer or Abacus sales.

events.title: Apple II and S-100 expansion products launch

actions.description: Logix launches the existing Apple II Expansion Card and FlexiDisk II plus three new products: S-100 FlexiBUS Interface, Apple II Video Card, and S-100 Video Card. Cards initially use AION chips. Native Apple drivers/examples and supported S-100 CP/M adapters accompany the cards; Apple participation does not imply an S-100 endorsement.
An Apple representative participates in the demonstration.

agreement_terms.description: Logix owns design, firmware, drivers, integration and sales. DRI’s optional CP/M interfaces support eligible S-100 systems but the card program is not a DRI obligation. No Apple CP/M execution is included.

actions.description: Microsoft releases Microsoft BASIC for Aurelia at NCC 1979 as licensed third-party software.

events.title: Model II CP/M, FlexiBUS and Abacus demonstrated at NCC

actions.description: Demonstrate Abacus using the native Model II display/keyboard, a CP/M disk build and qualified prototype FlexiBUS peripherals. Distinguish demonstrations from customer releases; announce an autumn supported 64 KB configuration. No Logix video subsystem is required.

events.title: NCC 1979 open architecture and migration presentation

actions.description: Present a 50-minute cross-vendor campaign before questions. Demonstrate applications/documents, then independent BPI, FlexiBUS, Apple native drivers and optional video. BPI management speaks with partners. State that the next generation breaks native Z80 binary compatibility; C source/API portability reduces migration work and a planned optional Z80 compatibility coprocessor supports qualified legacy software. Reveal neither processor word size nor architecture before NCC 1980. See ncc_1979_campaign.json. This day is a selected scenario milestone.

events.title: Detailed CP/M-80 compatibility module development begins

actions.description: Begin confidential implementation work following the public June 4 migration commitment and preliminary feasibility work. Public language remains a planned optional Z80 coprocessor for qualified legacy applications; implementation details and future-platform specifications remain undisclosed until NCC 1980. This is not a July shipment.

events.title: Confidential next-generation software and tool preparation

actions.description: Prepare future system software internally; publish no names or architectural details before NCC 1980.

Prepare application migration and future C tools internally. Public 1979 clinics use the established C environment and documented interfaces only; no future-target binaries, compiler output or SDK are distributed.

Confidentially benchmark Aurelia/Abacus business workflows, Tandy distribution and Apple software partnerships; examine price, training, service and independent OS suppliers. No public IBM product announcement or immediate buyer-deferral effect is assumed.

events.title: Compatibility roadshows and developer migration clinics

actions.description: Run dealer demonstrations, joint trade-press activity and developer clinics. Teach documented APIs, file interchange, C portability boundaries and device-class drivers. Publish a directory distinguishing shipping, qualified and prototype configurations. This day is a selected scenario milestone.

Competitive review increases priority for protecting existing software, peripherals and customer data in successor plans. This is a requirements decision, not a guaranteed technical fix or early Lisa/GUI shipment. Apple keeps its independent hardware roadmap.

Initial qualified SMC-manufactured chips become commercially available in the alternate timeline. This begins staged availability, not guaranteed release of every chip or mature yields; video RAM retains a separate qualification gate. SMC performs wafer fabrication rather than merely packaging AION dies.

outcomes.description: AION remains the launch supplier for June 1979 cards. Qualified SMC parts become independently purchasable alternatives; no automatic procurement switch, price reduction or high-volume yield is asserted.

events.title: Supported Model II CP/M and Abacus configuration released

actions.description: Scenario customer release within the historical October US shipping window: supported 64 KB CP/M configuration, Model II Abacus and the separately supported FlexiBUS option. Release follows disk, printing, save/reopen, native UI and interface qualification; publish resource limits. October 15 is a scenario-selected day. OEM economics and Tandy system prices are not inferred from Aurelia retail prices.

Promote the separately recorded Tandy customer release and only individually qualified SMC or peripheral products. Update directory evidence; do not imply all licensed chips, every peripheral class or new independent OEM systems are shipping. This day is a selected scenario milestone.

events.title: Aurelia+, Pulse, Abacus 2.0 and manufacturer compatibility kit arrive

participants.role: independent partner; head of BPI presents

actions.description: Launches Aurelia+.
Presents Pulse and Abacus 2.0.
Makes corresponding training available.

Launch the Aurelia Software Compatibility Kit with published contracts, reference runtime adapters, diagnostics and application acceptance tests. Manufacturers may independently implement the released environment; optional paid support and certification use standard terms. Application redistribution remains separately licensed.

Shift new hardware development and promotion to Aurelia+ while enabling independent Aurelia-class clones. Continue installed-base support and compatible software; do not impose an immediate Aurelia withdrawal. FlexiBUS and Logix video adoption remain separate choices. Future architecture details remain undisclosed until NCC 1980.

Present the 45-minute COMDEX campaign plus questions: More room to work. More freedom to choose. Run identical live calculated shaded-cube and Abacus workloads on Aurelia and Aurelia+ under equivalent conditions; show measured results without an unverified speed multiplier. See comdex_1979_campaign.json.

Demonstrate Abacus 2.0 charts and spreadsheet-linked layouts using precalculated fictitious employee values, then preview and print a complete payslip batch. The head of independent BPI follows Abacus with the source payroll and reconciled file-exchange workflow, and joins the partner segment. Abacus 2.0 also serves existing Aurelia owners.

Authorise a PC project because independent suppliers, including Logix, Tandy and Apple, are establishing business applications, interfaces and retail/service channels outside IBM. Do not assume a Logix–Apple duopoly. Initially expect external software to shorten development.

outcomes.description: DRI remains an independent licensor but its existing funded development and CP/M-80 commitments leave no committed x86 OS on IBM’s required schedule. Paterson’s recruitment removes the historical SCP 86-DOS route; Letwin’s absence reduces Microsoft staffing options. Alternatives remain possible. Supplier selection, substitute OS development and application qualification become the critical path toward early 1982, rather than technical impossibility.

agreement_terms.description: Functional prototype after project start. Hardware milestone only; it does not establish OS/application or commercial readiness.
Manufacturing-ready design after project start. Hardware milestone only; it does not establish OS/application or commercial readiness.

Early-1982 commercial target after supplier-selection delay, alternative OS development and business-application qualification. A late-1981 recovery remains possible; this is not a guarantee that no other OS can be produced.

effective_date.qualifier: Early in the year; planned target, not a completed launch

agreement_terms.description: Approximately this price for an entry configuration; practical business systems cost more.

actions.description: Target Tandy shipping, one additional named OEM selling a supported CP/M-extension/FlexiBUS option, another OEM in qualification, dealer/integrator configurations and third-party devices in several categories. These are adoption targets, not recorded achievements or contracted orders. This day is a selected scenario milestone.

events.title: Customer evidence and compatibility programme review

actions.description: Publish verified customer examples, compatibility results and partner configurations. Target three to five non-Logix manufacturers with supported configurations by NCC 1980, counting Tandy once and excluding duplicate dealer builds. Do not disclose the new processor architecture early. This day is a selected scenario milestone.

events.title: IBM software sourcing review exposes schedule gap

actions.description: Supplier discussions find no committed qualified x86 CP/M delivery on IBM terms. DRI prioritises AIONix and existing CP/M-80 OEM obligations rather than refusing solely because IBM competes with Logix. Microsoft cannot acquire the historical Paterson/SCP product in this scenario and must recruit, commission or obtain another OS.
Start a package with simplified setup, Apple II-oriented interface, documentation and support.

outcomes.description: Accounting coverage potentially includes general ledger, receivables/payables, inventory, invoicing and payroll.

phases.title: Artemis launch, compatibility card and recompiled products

actions.description: Launch Artemis with AIONix, peripherals, expansions, developer tooling and support.
Introduces Artemis training.

At NCC 1980 reveal the processor architecture and word size withheld in the NCC 1979 public campaign. The separately sold Z80 compatibility module is an optional qualified legacy path; native applications require an appropriate target build.

Released Artemis application binaries using documented, supported ERA/AIONix interfaces retain a supported execution path on subsequent Logix professional platforms through 2000: native execution, a maintained compatibility runtime, or emulation. Source portability is a separate commitment, not a substitute for the binary execution path.

Demonstrate familiar multitasking, separate ERA/Z80 C builds and qualified legacy-card execution; compare verified vector calculations on Aurelia+, PDP-11/34 and Artemis before revealing the 32-bit RISC ERA 1 architecture. Publish only measured performance.
The head of independent BPI Systems presents after Abacus and joins the partner section; BPI retains separate branding, licences, support and receipts.

Ship Artemis 128 with a replaceable 16 KiB video card and Mono II or Color II; ship Artemis 256 with 32 AION 64 Kbit system RAM chips, a 32 KiB video card and Mono Pro or Color II. Both cards include 1 KiB exclusive sprite SRAM. Only the professional card and Mono Pro enable 640×400 modes; Color II keeps legacy timings. High-resolution demonstrations and paid follow-up campaign are separately budgeted; production qualification remains required.

outcomes.description: Launch campaign and dated follow-up activities are specified in ncc_1980_campaign.json and NCC_1980_CAMPAIGN.md. Compatibility through 2000 is a commitment with eligibility and maintenance obligations, not evidence of future fulfilment.

events.title: IBM funds an alternative OS delivery programme

actions.description: After evaluating suppliers, fund substitute OS work and stabilise application interfaces. Supplier identity and OS name remain unresolved. Hardware development proceeds; development, utilities, application ports and service preparation now determine commercial timing.

events.title: AION shifts major software development to 32-bit Artemis

actions.description: Presents Artemis-exclusive Abacus 3.0 and Pulse 3.0; makes Artemis the main target for major development.

COMDEX follow-up to the Artemis campaign: publish native software demonstrations and compatibility progress while preserving Aurelia/Aurelia+ maintenance and independent manufacturers’ compatibility programme.

outcomes.description: Aurelia receives maintenance and simplified refreshes.

phases.title: Artemis Pro, Networking and new BPI

actions.description: Presents TCP/IP networking, Artemis PRO and Aurelia/Artemis network upgrades.
Introduces a client-server generation built around a robust relational database.

outcomes.description: Networking becomes the standard Artemis direction rather than an isolated peripheral.

events.title: IBM business-software qualification delays commercial release

actions.description: Hardware is substantially ready but OS integration, business-application qualification and support preparation remain on the critical path. Retain early 1982 as the planned commercial launch, with late 1981 possible if issues are resolved unusually quickly; no completed 1982 shipment is asserted.
Studies for a bachelor degree in economics at Harvard.
